summary: Predecessor phase '...1.1R' stopped BLOCKED (C-1: production human-principal/credential registries empty). This phase performed exactly the missing deployment-owner bootstrap and nothing more. Source inspection established bootstrap requires two deployment-owner-only ceremonies, not one: scripts/hpac_protected_root_admin.py enroll-principal (creates the mechanism-neutral PrincipalRecord -- hpac_principal_admin.py's enroll-first-credential requires an already-active principal per human_principal_registry.py _require_active_principal) then scripts/hpac_principal_admin.py enroll-first-credential (real CTAP2 makeCredential against the genuine YubiKey, atomic CredentialRecord+sidecar+counter-state write). Both were run once each by the operator. Two environmental (non-code) issues were hit and resolved during the ceremony: sudo inherited the operator's interactive-shell PATH, which has agent-writable directories ahead of /bin, tripping the fail-closed ACL-trust-tool resolver in hatp_class_b_topology_verifier.py (fixed with a minimal PATH via env -i); the resulting env -i also cleared HOME, breaking Python's user-site resolution of the fido2 package (fixed with an explicit PYTHONPATH). Independent post-write verification was obtained via plain filesystem cat/ls as root (bypasses the Python HPACStoreAuthority layer entirely): principal-registry.json shows exactly 1 active principal (hp-8cee9b36b6784608ae48261af86289b8) and 1 active credential (hpc-2e7bbfa0c1b2480ba84ab5792159179d, mechanism hpac.fido2.uv_presence.v2, rp_id hpac.pcae.local, transports usb, aaguid b7d3f68e88a6471e9ecf2df26d041ede matching the previously hardware-verified genuine YubiKey); the credentials/ directory has exactly one credential subdirectory with exactly the three expected files (fido2-credential.json, counter-state.json, enrollment-evidence.json), all cross-checking exactly (raw_credential_id_digest identical between the CLI output, the sidecar, and the enrollment evidence; public_key identical between registry and sidecar). A first attempt at an independent read via a fresh ad hoc script calling HumanPrincipalRegistryStore.production() directly (rather than through raw filesystem access) correctly failed closed with HPACAuthorityError ('production HPAC root is not protected from the configured agent principal (root=agent_is_owner_with_write_bit)') because _validate_production_boundary() falls back to the live process's own ambient identity (root, since the script itself was run under sudo) when no production_writer() transaction has bound the configured-agent identity -- this is a genuine architectural gap (no canonical read-only, boundary-safe inspection path exists outside a mutating transaction) recorded as a finding, not repaired (would require a src/pcae change, out of this phase's scope), and not routed around by inventing new authority. No protected APPROVE/REJECT election, no presentation evidence, no certification getAssertion, no require_real_assurance=True call, no PRODUCTION AuthenticatedHumanPrincipal, no Gate 5 certification were performed. Runtime confirmed unchanged (not_implemented/Observed/observe/unavailable, 0 plugins/capabilities) after the ceremony. C-1: RESOLVED. F-5: DEPLOYMENT VERIFIED -- FINAL CERTIFICATION PENDING. N-16-5: NOT CLOSED (unchanged -- no certification ceremony performed here). N-16-6/N-16-7 remain OPEN/UNTOUCHED and strictly out of scope. A fresh N-16-5 certification retry successor is derived (not begun).
